schema: Confessiones gloss overrides. Keyed by the exact lexicon key (lowercase printed form). Each value is an `edited` card the reader shows on click: { lemma?, pos?, gloss, note? }. Where `lemma`/`pos` are omitted the entry keeps Whitaker's. Notes cite book.chapter (Conf. 1.1 = Liber I Caput 1). This is a STARTER set — refine glosses against latin.md before treating them as final.

confessio.gloss: confession — both praise of God and admission of sin; the double work of this book.
confessio.note: Conf. 1.1: Augustine confesses God's greatness and his own unlikeness. Unlike the psalter's 'confessio' as thanksgiving, here both senses run together.

confessiones.gloss: confessions (pl.) — the title: praises and self-disclosures before God.
confessiones.note: The work's own name. Book 10 asks what he is doing in these confessiones before many witnesses.

confessionem.gloss: confession (acc.) — the act of speaking before God.

confessione.note: Conf. 10.1: he wants to do the truth 'in confessione'.

confiteor.gloss: I confess — I praise Thee, and I tell what I have been.
confiteor.note: The book's governing verb. Conf. 1.6: 'confiteor tibi, domine caeli et terrae'.

confitear.gloss: let me confess / I may confess (subj.).

confitebor.gloss: I will confess / I will praise.

confiteri.gloss: to confess — to speak the truth of oneself before God.

inquietum.gloss: restless — the heart that cannot rest until it rests in God.
inquietum.note: Conf. 1.1: 'inquietum est cor nostrum donec requiescat in te' — the book's first and most famous sentence.

requiescat.gloss: it may rest — rest as the end of the restless heart.
requiescat.note: Conf. 1.1, paired with inquietum cor. Not mere sleep: repose in God.

cor.gloss: heart — the inner self that is restless, remembers, and confesses.
cor.note: Conf. 1.1 'cor nostrum'; throughout, cor is where God is sought (not the chest as organ).

memoria.gloss: memory — the vast inner hall where Augustine searches for God (Book 10).
memoria.note: Conf. 10.8–25: memoria is not a storehouse of facts but the place of the self. 'ecce quantum spatiatus sum in memoria mea' (10.24).

caritas.gloss: charity, love — God's love, and the love that orders other loves.
caritas.note: Not classical 'dearness/costliness' first. Conf. 13 and the pear theft (2.4) turn on disordered love vs caritas.

consuetudo.gloss: habit, custom — the chain of old loves that holds the will (Book 8).
consuetudo.note: Conf. 8.5: consuetudo is the enemy of the new will. Not mere 'custom' in the social sense.

concupiscentia.gloss: concupiscence — disordered desire (1 John 2:16's three lusts in Book 10).
concupiscentia.note: Conf. 10.30–41: lust of the flesh, lust of the eyes, pride of life. Not a mild 'desire'.

continentia.gloss: continence — the gift of a gathered will; 'Give what Thou commandest'.
continentia.note: Conf. 8.11 and 10.29: 'da quod iubes et iube quod vis.' Continentia is God gathering the scattered self, not mere sexual abstinence.

temptatio.gloss: trial, temptation — the proving of the restless heart.
temptatio.note: O'Donnell writes temptatio (not tentatio). Conf. 10's long trial of the three concupiscences.

inluminatio.gloss: illumination — God as the light by which the mind sees.
inluminatio.note: Late spelling in- (classical ill-). Conf. 7's intellectual vision and 10: God is 'inluminatio mea'.

veritas.gloss: Truth — God himself, not a property of sentences.
veritas.note: Conf. 10.23–24: the happy life is joy in the truth; he finds God where he finds veritas.

pulchritudo.gloss: beauty — God as Beauty ever old and ever new.
pulchritudo.note: Conf. 10.27: 'sero te amavi, pulchritudo tam antiqua et tam nova'.

fornicatio.gloss: fornication — turning from God to creatures; not only the sexual sense.
fornicatio.note: Conf. 1.13: 'fornicabar abs te' — to love the creature without the Creator is fornication (cf. Ps 72).

sero.gloss: late, too late — the cry of Book 10.
sero.note: Conf. 10.27: 'sero te amavi' — 'too late loved I Thee' (Pusey).

amavi.gloss: I loved — of God, or of the wrong things.
amavi.note: Conf. 10.27 'sero te amavi'; Conf. 2.4 he loved the theft itself.

tolle.gloss: take up — the child's cry in the garden.
tolle.note: Conf. 8.12: 'tolle lege, tolle lege' — take up and read. The conversion of Book 8.

lege.gloss: read! (imperative) — paired with tolle in the garden.
lege.note: Conf. 8.12 'tolle lege'. Whitaker may also list lex, legis; here it is the verb.

recolens.gloss: recalling, going back over — memory's work in confession.
recolens.note: Conf. 2.1: 'recolens vias meas nequissimas'. Near the planned 'recolligere' (gathering the scattered self).

recordari.gloss: to remember — to call back into the heart.
recordari.note: See 'memoria'. Book 10 remembers in order to find God in memory.

magnus.gloss: great — first word of the Confessions, said of God.
magnus.note: Conf. 1.1: 'magnus es, domine, et laudabilis valde'.

laudabilis.gloss: praiseworthy — God is greatly to be praised.
laudabilis.note: Conf. 1.1, with magnus. The book begins in praise, not in narrative.

beata.gloss: happy, blessed — the beata vita, joy in the Truth.
beata.note: Conf. 10.20–23: everyone wants a happy life; it is gaudium de veritate.

voluntas.gloss: will — one man, two wills, in the garden of Book 8.
voluntas.note: Conf. 8.9–10: the monstrousness of a will that commands itself and is not obeyed.

superbia.gloss: pride — God resists the proud; the third concupiscence.
superbia.note: Conf. 1.1 cites 'superbis resistis'. Book 10's pride of life (ambitio saeculi).

humilitas.gloss: humility — the way of the Word who descended.
humilitas.note: Conf. 7.18: he could not return until he took the way of humilitas, Christ the mediator.

converte.gloss: turn (us) — conversion as being turned by God.
converte.note: Not only a moral U-turn: God turns the self. Cf. 'deus virtutum, converte nos'.
